title.zh: 卷三十六 蜀書六 關張馬黃趙傳
title.en: Volume 36: Book of Shu 6 - Biographies of Guan, Zhang, Ma, Huang, and Zhao
title.raw: 卷三十六 蜀書六 關張馬黃趙傳 Volume 36: Book of Shu 6 - Biographies of Guan, Zhang, Ma, Huang, and Zhao

sentences.zh: 關羽字雲長，本字長生，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Guan Yu, courtesy name Yunzhang, originally courtesy name Changsheng, was a native of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu, styled Yunzhang—his original style was Changsheng—came from Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 亡命奔涿郡。

translations.literal: He fled as an outlaw and ran to Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He fled the law and made his way to Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 先主於鄉里合徒眾，而羽與張飛為之禦侮。

translations.literal: When the First Lord gathered followers in his home district, Yu together with Zhang Fei defended him from insult and harm.
translations.idiomatic: While the First Lord was raising a band of men in his home country, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei stood as his shield against abuse and attack.

sentences.zh: 先主為平原相，以羽、飛為別部司馬，分統部曲。

translations.literal: When the First Lord became Administrator of Pingyuan, he appointed Yu and Fei as Separate Command Majors, each commanding a division of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Once the First Lord was appointed Administrator of Pingyuan, he made Guan Yu and Zhang Fei Separate Command Majors, splitting the command of their forces between them.

sentences.zh: 先主與二人寢則同床，恩若兄弟。

translations.literal: The First Lord with the two of them, when sleeping, shared one bed; their kindness was like that of brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord slept on the same couch with the two of them, and the affection among them was like that of brothers.

sentences.zh: 而稠人廣坐，侍立終日，隨先主周旋，不避艱險。

translations.literal: Yet in crowded places and at public gatherings they stood in attendance all day, following the First Lord in his comings and goings, not shunning hardship or danger.
translations.idiomatic: Even in thronged halls and before large assemblies they would stand attendance the whole day through, attending the First Lord wherever he went, never shrinking from hardship or peril.

sentences.zh: 〈蜀記曰：曹公與劉備圍呂布於下邳，關羽啟公，布使秦宜祿行求救，乞娶其妻，公許之。

translations.literal: The Shu Ji states: Lord Cao and Liu Bei besieged Lü Bu at Xiapi. Guan Yu reported to the Lord that, when Lü Bu had Qin Yilu go out to seek rescue, he begged to marry Qin's wife, and the Lord granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Ji records that when Lord Cao and Liu Bei had Lü Bu bottled up at Xiapi, Guan Yu petitioned him: Lü Bu had sent Qin Yilu out to plead for help, and Guan Yu asked leave to take Qin's wife in marriage; Lord Cao agreed.

sentences.zh: 臨破，又屢啟於公。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall, he repeatedly reported to the Lord.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was on the verge of being taken, he pressed the matter again and again with Lord Cao.

sentences.zh: 公疑其有異色，先遣迎看，因自留之，羽心不自安。

translations.literal: The Lord suspected she had unusual beauty, first sent men to meet and look at her, and therefore kept her himself; Yu's heart was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao suspected the woman was strikingly beautiful, sent someone ahead to fetch and inspect her, then kept her for himself—leaving Guan Yu uneasy in his mind.

sentences.zh: 此與魏氏春秋所說無異也。〉

translations.literal: This is no different from what the Wei shi chunqiu says.
translations.idiomatic: This matches the account given in the Wei shi chunqiu.

sentences.zh: 先主之襲殺徐州刺史車胄，使羽守下邳城，行太守事，

translations.literal: When the First Lord suddenly attacked and killed the Inspector of Xu Province, Che Zhou, he had Yu guard Xiapi city and act as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Lord struck down Xu Province Inspector Che Zhou in a surprise attack, he left Guan Yu to hold Xiapi and conduct the duties of Administrator.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》云：以羽領徐州。〉

translations.literal: The Wei shu states: Yu was placed in charge of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu adds that Guan Yu was given authority over Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 而身還小沛。

translations.literal: While he himself returned to Xiao Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord himself meanwhile withdrew to Xiao Pei.

sentences.zh: 建安五年，曹公東征，先主奔袁紹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jian'an, Lord Cao campaigned east; the First Lord fled to Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 5, when Lord Cao marched east, the First Lord broke away to Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 曹公禽羽以歸，拜為偏將軍，禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: Lord Cao captured Yu and brought him back, appointed him Lieutenant General, and treated him with very great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao took Guan Yu captive and brought him back, named him Lieutenant General, and honored him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 紹遣大將軍顏良攻東郡太守劉延於白馬，曹公使張遼及羽為先鋒擊之。

translations.literal: Shao sent Grand General Yan Liang to attack Grand Administrator of Dongjun Liu Yan at Baima; Lord Cao ordered Zhang Liao and Yu to serve as vanguard and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao dispatched Grand General Yan Liang against Dongjun Grand Administrator Liu Yan at Baima; Lord Cao sent Zhang Liao and Guan Yu ahead as the van to engage him.

sentences.zh: 羽望見良麾蓋，策馬刺良於萬眾之中，斬其首還，紹諸將莫能當者，遂解白馬圍。

translations.literal: Yu saw Liang's command banner and canopy, spurred his horse and thrust Liang amid ten thousand men, cut off his head and returned; none of Shao's generals could withstand him, and so the siege of Baima was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu spotted Yan Liang's command canopy, drove his horse into the mass of the enemy, ran Yan Liang through, and came back with his head; none of Yuan Shao's officers could stop him, and the investment of Baima was broken.

sentences.zh: 曹公即表封羽為漢壽亭侯。

translations.literal: Lord Cao immediately memorialized and enfeoffed Yu as Marquis of Hanshou village.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao at once submitted a memorial enfeoffing Guan Yu as Marquis of Hanshou precinct.

sentences.zh: 初，曹公壯羽為人，而察其心神無久留之意，謂張遼曰：「卿試以情問之。

translations.literal: At first, Lord Cao admired Yu's character as a man, but observed that in his heart and spirit he had no intention of staying long; he said to Zhang Liao, "You try asking him with sincere feeling."
translations.idiomatic: From the first, Lord Cao respected Guan Yu as a man, yet he saw that Guan Yu's heart was not here to stay. He told Zhang Liao, "See if you can sound him out, personally and in earnest."

sentences.zh: 」既而遼以問羽，羽歎曰：「吾極知曹公待我厚，然吾受劉將軍厚恩，誓以共死，不可背之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liao asked Yu; Yu sighed and said, "I know very well that Lord Cao treats me generously, yet I have received deep kindness from General Liu and have sworn to die with him; I cannot betray him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao put the question to him. Guan Yu sighed and said, "I know full well how generously Lord Cao has treated me, but I owe General Liu Bei a profound debt and have sworn to share death with him; I cannot turn my back on that."

sentences.zh: 吾終不留，吾要當立效以報曹公乃去。

translations.literal: I will in the end not stay; I must establish merit to repay Lord Cao and then depart.
translations.idiomatic: I will not remain here forever: I mean to earn a deed of service to repay Lord Cao, and then I shall go."

sentences.zh: 」遼以羽言報曹公，曹公義之。

translations.literal: Liao reported Yu's words to Lord Cao; Lord Cao deemed him righteous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao relayed Guan Yu's words to Lord Cao, who pronounced him a man of honor.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：遼欲白太祖，恐太祖殺羽，不白，非事君之道，乃歎曰：「公，君父也；

translations.literal: The Fu zi states: Liao wished to report to the Grand Progenitor, but feared the Grand Progenitor would kill Yu; not to report would fail the way of serving a lord; therefore he sighed and said, "The Lord is lord and father;
translations.idiomatic: The Fu zi records that Zhang Liao meant to inform the Grand Progenitor but feared he would put Guan Yu to death; to stay silent would violate the duty of a minister. He sighed, "The lord is father and sovereign to me;

sentences.zh: 羽，兄弟耳。

translations.literal: Yu is like a brother."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu is as a brother to me."

sentences.zh: 」遂白之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reported it.
translations.idiomatic: So he spoke up and told him.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「事君不忘其本，天下義士也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said, "Serving a lord yet not forgetting one's roots—he is a righteous knight of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor said, "To serve one's lord without forgetting where one came from—that is a true man of principle under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 度何時能去？

translations.literal: Estimate when he can leave?"
translations.idiomatic: When do you think he will actually leave?"

sentences.zh: 」遼曰：「羽受公恩，必立效報公而後去也。」〉

translations.literal: Liao said, "Yu has received the Lord's grace; he must establish merit to repay the Lord and afterward depart.""
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao replied, "Guan Yu has received your grace; he is bound to repay you with a feat of arms before he goes."

sentences.zh: 及羽殺顏良，曹公知其必去，重加賞賜。

translations.literal: When Yu had killed Yan Liang, Lord Cao knew he would certainly leave and heaped additional rewards on him.
translations.idiomatic: After Guan Yu slew Yan Liang, Lord Cao knew he would leave and showered him with further gifts.

sentences.zh: 羽盡封其所賜，拜書告辭，而奔先主於袁軍。

translations.literal: Yu sealed up everything he had been granted, bowed in writing to announce his farewell, and ran to join the First Lord in Yuan Shao's army.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu locked away every gift he had received, left a letter of parting, and rode off to rejoin the First Lord in Yuan Shao's host.

sentences.zh: 左右欲追之，曹公曰：「彼各為其主，勿追也。」

translations.literal: Those around him wished to pursue him; Lord Cao said, "Each serves his own lord; do not pursue."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants wanted to give chase, but Lord Cao said, "Each man serves his own master. Let him go."

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以為曹公知羽不留而心嘉其志，去不遣追以成其義，自非有王霸之度，孰能至於此乎？

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi considers: Lord Cao knew Yu would not stay yet in his heart approved his intent; he let him go and did not send pursuit to complete his righteousness—unless one had the measure of a king or hegemon, who could reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks: Lord Cao knew Guan Yu would not remain, yet he honored the man's purpose, let him depart, and forbade pursuit so as to crown his integrity—only a ruler with true kingly breadth could rise to that.

sentences.zh: 斯實曹公之休美。〉

translations.literal: This was indeed a fine trait in Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: That was one of Lord Cao's finer moments.

sentences.zh: 從先主就劉表。

translations.literal: He followed the First Lord to join Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the First Lord in attaching himself to Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 表卒，曹公定荊州，先主自樊將南渡江，別遣羽乘船數百艘會江陵。

translations.literal: When Biao died, Lord Cao settled Jing Province; the First Lord, from Fan, was about to cross the river south, separately sent Yu with several hundred ships to rendezvous at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Biao died and Lord Cao took Jing Province, the First Lord set out from Fan to cross the Yangzi to the south, while detaching Guan Yu with several hundred boats to meet him at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 曹公追至當陽長阪，先主斜趣漢津，適與羽船相值，共至夏口。

translations.literal: Lord Cao pursued to Chang Slope of Dangyang; the First Lord angled toward Han Ford, happened to meet Yu's boats, and together they reached Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao's pursuit caught up at Changban Slope in Dangyang; the First Lord angled for Han Ford and there ran into Guan Yu's flotilla; together they made for Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 〈蜀記曰：初，劉備在許，與曹公共獵。

translations.literal: The Shu Ji states: At first, when Liu Bei was at Xu, he went hunting together with Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Ji says that early on, while Liu Bei was at Xu, he joined Lord Cao on a hunt.

sentences.zh: 獵中，眾散，羽勸備殺公，備不從。

translations.literal: During the hunt the company scattered; Yu urged Bei to kill the Lord; Bei did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the course of the hunt the party scattered, and Guan Yu urged Liu Bei to strike Lord Cao down; Liu Bei refused.

sentences.zh: 及在夏口，飄颻江渚，羽怒曰：「往日獵中，若從羽言，可無今日之困。

translations.literal: When they were at Xiakou, drifting on the river islets, Yu angrily said, "In the hunt of other days, had you followed Yu's words, there would not be today's distress.
translations.idiomatic: Later, adrift among the sandbars at Xiakou, Guan Yu said in anger, "Had you listened to me that day in the hunt, we would not be in this plight today."

sentences.zh: 」備曰：「是時亦為國家惜之耳；

translations.literal: Bei said, "At that time I also cherished the realm for the sake of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei answered, "Even then I was thinking of the altars of the land—

sentences.zh: 若天道輔正，安知此不為福邪！

translations.literal: if Heaven's way assists the right, how do we know this is not fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: if Heaven favors the just, who is to say this misfortune will not turn to our good?"

sentences.zh: 」臣松之以為備後與董承等結謀，但事泄不克諧耳，若為國家惜曹公，其如此言何！

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi considers that afterward Bei plotted with Dong Cheng and others, only the affair leaked and could not succeed; if it was for the state that he cherished Lord Cao, how does one explain such words as these!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi observes that Liu Bei later conspired with Dong Cheng and the rest; the plot simply leaked before it could succeed. If he had truly "spared Lord Cao for the sake of the state," how could he have spoken as he did here?

sentences.zh: 羽若果有此勸而備不肯從者，將以曹公腹心親戚，實繁有徒，事不宿構，非造次所行；

translations.literal: If Yu truly gave such counsel and Bei was unwilling to follow, it was because Cao had trusted intimates and kinsmen in great numbers; the matter was not prepared overnight and could not be carried out on the spur of the moment;
translations.idiomatic: If Guan Yu did urge assassination and Liu Bei held back, it was because Lord Cao's household and inner circle were numerous and close at hand; nothing had been laid in advance, and a rash stroke could not have been brought off;

sentences.zh: 曹雖可殺，身必不免，故以計而止，何惜之有乎！

translations.literal: though Cao might have been killed, he himself could not have escaped harm; therefore he stopped out of calculation—what "cherishing" was there!
translations.idiomatic: even had Lord Cao died, Liu Bei himself would not have walked away alive—so he checked himself by design. Where is the "sparing" in that?

sentences.zh: 既往之事，故讬為雅言耳。〉

translations.literal: It was a past matter; therefore he put it off with lofty words."
translations.idiomatic: It was water under the bridge, and he dressed it up in high-minded language."

sentences.zh: 孫權遣兵佐先主拒曹公，曹公引軍退歸。

translations.literal: Sun Quan sent troops to assist the First Lord in resisting Lord Cao; Lord Cao led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan dispatched troops to reinforce the First Lord against Lord Cao, and Lord Cao withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 先主收江南諸郡，乃封拜元勳，以羽為襄陽太守、蕩寇將軍，駐江北。

translations.literal: The First Lord gathered the commanderies south of the Long River and then enfeoffed and promoted the chief founders of merit, appointing Yu as Grand Administrator of Xiangyang and General Who Sweeps the Bandits, stationed north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord took the southern shore commanderies, he rewarded his principal founders, naming Guan Yu Grand Administrator of Xiangyang and General Who Sweeps the Bandits, with his camp on the north bank.

sentences.zh: 先主西定益州，拜羽董督荊州事。

translations.literal: When the First Lord pacified Yi Province in the west, he appointed Yu to supervise overall Jing Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Lord secured Yi Province to the west, he put Guan Yu in charge of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 羽聞馬超來降，舊非故人，羽書與諸葛亮，問超人才可誰比類。

translations.literal: When Yu heard that Ma Chao had come to surrender, not being an old acquaintance, Yu wrote to Zhuge Liang asking to what sort of man Chao's talents might be compared.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Ma Chao had surrendered—no old friend of his—Guan Yu wrote to Zhuge Liang asking what class of man Ma Chao's abilities belonged to.

sentences.zh: 亮知羽護前，乃答之曰：「孟起兼資文武，雄烈過人，一世之傑，黥、彭之徒，當與益德並驅爭先，猶未及髯之絕倫逸群也。

translations.literal: Liang knew Yu guarded his precedence; therefore he answered him, "Mengqi combines civil and martial gifts; his fierce valor surpasses others; he is a hero of the age, in the line of Qing Bu and Peng Yue; he may race neck and neck with Yide for first place, yet he still does not reach the Beard's peerless standing above the crowd."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang knew Guan Yu was touchy about rank, so he replied, "Mengqi unites the pen and the sword; his martial dash is extraordinary—a champion of the age, in the mold of Qing Bu or Peng Yue. He might vie with Yide for the lead, but he is still not the equal of your Lordship's magnificent beard, set apart from every other man."

sentences.zh: 」羽美鬚髯，故亮謂之髯。

translations.literal: Yu had a handsome beard; therefore Liang called him the Beard.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu was famed for his fine beard, which is why Zhuge Liang called him "the Beard."

sentences.zh: 羽省書大悅，以示賓客。

translations.literal: When Yu read the letter he was greatly pleased and showed it to his guests.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu read the letter with immense satisfaction and passed it around to his guests.

sentences.zh: 羽嘗為流矢所中，貫其左臂，後創雖愈，每至陰雨，骨常疼痛，醫曰：「矢鏃有毒，毒入於骨，當破臂作創，刮骨去毒，然後此患乃除耳。

translations.literal: Yu once was struck by a stray arrow that pierced his left arm; though the wound later healed, whenever the weather turned overcast and rainy the bone often ached; the physician said, "The arrowhead was poisoned; the poison has entered the bone; you must split the arm to open the wound, scrape the bone to remove the poison, and then this affliction can be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu had once been hit by a stray shaft that transfixed his left arm. The wound closed, but whenever the sky turned gray and wet the bone throbbed. The surgeon told him, "The point carried venom; the venom has entered the bone. We must lay open the arm, cut to the bone, and scrape the poison away—only then will the pain end."

sentences.zh: 」羽便伸臂令醫劈之。

translations.literal: Yu then extended his arm and ordered the physician to cleave it.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu simply stretched out his arm and told the surgeon to cut.

sentences.zh: 時羽適請諸將飲食相對，臂血流離，盈於盤器，而羽割炙引酒，言笑自若。

translations.literal: At the time Yu happened to be inviting the various generals to drink and eat face to face; blood poured from the arm and overflowed the plates and vessels, yet Yu carved roast meat and raised wine, talking and laughing as usual.
translations.idiomatic: He happened to be feasting his officers face to face: blood streamed from the arm and ran over the platters, yet he carved the roast, lifted his cup, and chatted and laughed as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，先主為漢中王，拜羽為前將軍，假節鉞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the First Lord became King of Hanzhong and appointed Yu as Forward General, granting him the credentials of office and the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the First Lord was made King of Hanzhong and named Guan Yu Forward General, investing him with the imperial baton and axe.

sentences.zh: 是歲，羽率眾攻曹仁於樊。

translations.literal: That year, Yu led the host to attack Cao Ren at Fan.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Guan Yu led his army against Cao Ren at Fan.

sentences.zh: 曹公遣于禁助仁。

translations.literal: Lord Cao sent Yu Jin to assist Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao dispatched Yu Jin to reinforce Cao Ren.

sentences.zh: 秋，大霖雨，漢水汎溢，禁所督七軍皆沒。

translations.literal: In autumn there was great continuous rain; the Han River rose and overflowed; all seven armies that Jin commanded were drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn the rains would not stop; the Han River burst its banks and drowned the seven corps Yu Jin commanded.

sentences.zh: 禁降羽，羽又斬將軍龐德。

translations.literal: Jin surrendered to Yu; Yu also beheaded General Pang De.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin capitulated to Guan Yu, who also executed General Pang De.

sentences.zh: 梁、郟、陸渾群盜或遙受羽印號，為之支黨，羽威震華夏。

translations.literal: Bandit gangs in Liang, Jia, and Luhun, some from afar received Yu's seals and titles and became his partisans; Yu's might shook the Huaxia heartland.
translations.idiomatic: Outlaws in Liang, Jia, and Luhun accepted his commissions from a distance and rallied to his banner; Guan Yu's name struck terror through the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 曹公議徙許都以避其銳，司馬宣王、蔣濟以為關羽得志，孫權必不原也。

translations.literal: Lord Cao debated moving the capital from Xu to avoid his sharpness; Sima Yi the King of Xuan and Jiang Ji held that, with Guan Yu's success, Sun Quan would certainly not be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao considered shifting the court from Xu to escape his momentum; Sima Yi (later King Xuan) and Jiang Ji argued that once Guan Yu had his way, Sun Quan would never stomach it.

sentences.zh: 可遣人勸權躡其後，許割江南以封權，則樊圍自解。

translations.literal: One could send a man to urge Quan to tread on his rear, promising to carve out the south of the Long River and enfeoff Quan, and then the siege of Fan would of itself be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed sending someone to prompt Sun Quan to stab him in the back, with a pledge to cede the south of the Long River as Sun Quan's fief—then the ring around Fan would break of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 曹公從之。

translations.literal: Lord Cao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao took their advice.

sentences.zh: 先是，權遣使為子索羽女，羽罵辱其使，不許婚，權大怒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Quan had sent an envoy to ask for Yu's daughter for his son; Yu reviled and insulted the envoy, refusing the marriage; Quan was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Quan had sent an envoy to ask for Guan Yu's daughter for his son; Guan Yu abused the messenger and rejected the match, enraging Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：羽圍樊，權遣使求助之，敕使莫速進，又遣主簿先致命於羽。

translations.literal: The Dian lue states: When Yu besieged Fan, Quan sent an envoy to ask him for help, ordering the envoy not to advance quickly, and also sent a chief clerk ahead to deliver his message to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Dian lue says that while Guan Yu besieged Fan, Sun Quan sent an envoy offering help but ordered him not to hurry forward, and first sent a chief clerk ahead to announce himself to Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽忿其淹遲，又自已得於禁等，乃罵曰：「鰂子敢爾，如使樊城拔，吾不能滅汝邪！

translations.literal: Yu was angry at his delay, and moreover since he himself had captured Yu Jin and the others, he reviled him, saying, "You rat-spawn dare thus; if Fan city is taken, can I not destroy you!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu resented the deliberate slowness and, flush with his capture of Yu Jin and the rest, cursed him: "You wretched cur—dare you treat me so? Once Fan falls, do you think I cannot wipe you out?"

sentences.zh: 」權聞之，知其輕己，偽手書以謝羽，許以自往。

translations.literal: When Quan heard it, he knew Yu slighted himself; he forged a letter in his own hand to apologize to Yu and promised to come in person.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan heard this and knew Guan Yu despised him; he forged a personal letter of apology and promised to come himself.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以為荊、吳雖外睦，而內相猜防，故權之襲羽，潛師密發。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi considers that, although Jing and Wu were outwardly cordial, inwardly they suspected and guarded against each other; therefore Quan's strike against Yu was a hidden army sent in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Jingzhou and Wu were allies in name but eyed each other warily within—hence Sun Quan's blow at Guan Yu was a strike launched in stealth.

sentences.zh: 按呂蒙傳雲：「伏精兵於□冓□鹿之中，使白衣搖櫓，作商賈服。

translations.literal: According to Lü Meng's biography it states, "He concealed crack troops in the narrows (text damaged) among the reeds, had men in white shake the oars, and dress as merchants."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng's biography says he hid picked troops in a concealed reach of the waterway (the manuscript is damaged here), put men in white to pull the oars, and disguised them as traders.

sentences.zh: 」以此言之，羽不求助於權，權必不語羽當往也。

translations.literal: Speaking from this, Yu did not seek help from Quan, and Quan certainly would not have told Yu he was coming.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows: Guan Yu never begged aid from Sun Quan, nor would Sun Quan have announced his own approach to Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 若許相援助，何故匿其形跡乎？〉

translations.literal: If he had promised mutual assistance, why hide his tracks?"
translations.idiomatic: If he had truly meant to help, why conceal his movements?"

sentences.zh: 又南郡太守麋芳在江陵，將軍士仁屯公安，素皆嫌羽輕己。

translations.literal: Moreover Grand Administrator of Nan commandery Mi Fang was at Jiangling, and General Shi Ren was stationed at Gong'an; both had long resented Yu's slighting them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Nan commandery Grand Administrator Mi Fang held Jiangling and General Shi Ren garrisoned Gong'an; both had long nursed a grudge because Guan Yu looked down on them.

sentences.zh: 羽之出軍，芳、仁供給軍資，不悉相救。

translations.literal: When Yu marched out on campaign, Fang and Ren supplied military stores but did not fully meet the relief required.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Yu took the field, Mi Fang and Shi Ren provisioned the army but fell short of what was needed.

sentences.zh: 羽言「還當治之」，芳、仁咸懷懼不安。

translations.literal: Yu said, "When I return I shall deal with them"; Fang and Ren both harbored fear and were uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu said, "When I come back I shall settle accounts with them"—words that left Mi Fang and Shi Ren terrified.

sentences.zh: 於是權陰誘芳、仁，芳、仁使人迎權。

translations.literal: Thereupon Quan secretly enticed Fang and Ren; Fang and Ren sent men to welcome Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan then secretly won them over, and they sent agents to receive him.

sentences.zh: 而曹公遣徐晃救曹仁，

translations.literal: Meanwhile Lord Cao sent Xu Huang to rescue Cao Ren,
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Lord Cao sent Xu Huang to relieve Cao Ren,

sentences.zh: 〈蜀記曰：羽與晃宿相愛，遙共語，但說平生，不及軍事。

translations.literal: The Shu Ji states: Yu and Huang had long been fond of each other; from afar they conversed together, speaking only of their whole lives, not touching military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Ji records that Guan Yu and Xu Huang had long been close; they hailed each other from a distance and spoke only of old times, never of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 須臾，晃下馬宣令：「得關雲長頭，賞金千斤。

translations.literal: After a moment Huang dismounted and proclaimed the order, "Whoever obtains Guan Yunzhang's head will be rewarded a thousand jin of gold."
translations.idiomatic: Presently Xu Huang dismounted and read out the order: "The man who brings me Guan Yu's head gets a thousand jin of gold."

sentences.zh: 」羽驚怖，謂晃曰：「大兄，是何言邪！

translations.literal: Yu was shocked and frightened, and said to Huang, "Elder brother, what words are these!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu started and said to him, "Elder brother—what kind of talk is that?"

sentences.zh: 」晃曰：「此國之事耳。」〉

translations.literal: Huang said, "This is the state's affair.""
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang replied, "This is state business, not private friendship."

sentences.zh: 羽不能克，引軍退還。

translations.literal: Yu could not overcome him and led the army back in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu could not break him and drew his troops off.

sentences.zh: 權已據江陵，盡虜羽士眾妻子，羽軍遂散。

translations.literal: Quan had already occupied Jiangling and captured all of Yu's soldiers' wives and children; Yu's army thereupon scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had already seized Jiangling and taken every wife and child of Guan Yu's men; the army melted away.

sentences.zh: 權遣將逆擊羽，斬羽及子平於臨沮。

translations.literal: Quan sent a general to intercept and strike Yu, beheading Yu and his son Ping at Linju.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent a general to intercept Guan Yu and cut him down, together with his son Guan Ping, at Linju.

sentences.zh: 〈蜀記曰：權遣將軍擊羽，獲羽及子平。

translations.literal: The Shu Ji states: Quan sent a general to attack Yu, capturing Yu and Ping.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Ji says Sun Quan sent a general against Guan Yu and took Guan Yu and Guan Ping alive.

sentences.zh: 權欲活羽以敵劉、曹，左右曰：「狼子不可養，後必為害。

translations.literal: Quan wished to keep Yu alive to oppose Liu and Cao; those around him said, "A wolf's cub cannot be reared; afterward it will surely become a harm.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan thought of sparing Guan Yu to use him against Liu Bei and Lord Cao, but his attendants said, "You cannot raise a wolf's whelp—it will only harm you later.

sentences.zh: 曹公不即除之，自取大患，乃議徙都。

translations.literal: Lord Cao did not at once remove him and himself drew a great calamity; then he debated moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao failed to kill him at once and reaped disaster for it—even talked of moving the capital.

sentences.zh: 今豈可生！

translations.literal: How can he now be allowed to live!"
translations.idiomatic: How can we let this man live?"

sentences.zh: 」乃斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: So they put him to death.

sentences.zh: 臣松之按吳書：孫權遣將潘璋逆斷羽走路，羽至即斬，且臨沮去江陵二三百里，豈容不時殺羽，方議其生死乎？

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi checks the Wu shu: Sun Quan sent General Pan Zhang to intercept and cut off Yu's escape route; when Yu arrived he was beheaded at once; moreover Linju is two or three hundred li from Jiangling—how could there have been time not to kill Yu at once and only then debate whether he lived or died?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi checked the Wu shu: Sun Quan sent General Pan Zhang to block Guan Yu's retreat and beheaded him as soon as he arrived. Linju lies two or three hundred li from Jiangling—there was no interval for arguing his fate before the blade fell.

sentences.zh: 又云「權欲活羽以敵劉、曹」，此之不然，可以絕智者之口。

translations.literal: It also says "Quan wished to keep Yu alive to oppose Liu and Cao"—this is not so and can shut the mouths of the clever.
translations.idiomatic: The claim that "Sun Quan wished to spare Guan Yu to play him against Liu and Cao" does not hold up; it should silence those who fancy themselves clever.

sentences.zh: 吳曆曰：權送羽首於曹公，以諸侯禮葬其屍骸。〉

translations.literal: The Wu li states: Quan sent Yu's head to Lord Cao and buried his remains with the rites due a feudal lord."
translations.idiomatic: The Wu li records that Sun Quan sent Guan Yu's head to Lord Cao and interred his body with the ceremony owed a feudal lord."

sentences.zh: 追諡羽曰壯繆侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhuangmou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously canonized as Marquis Zhuangmou.

sentences.zh: 〈蜀記曰：羽初出軍圍樊，夢豬齧其足，語子平曰：「吾今年衰矣，然不得還！

translations.literal: The Shu Ji states: When Yu first marched out to besiege Fan, he dreamed a pig gnawed his foot; he said to his son Ping, "I am in decline this year; yet I cannot return!"
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Ji says that when Guan Yu first marched to invest Fan, he dreamed a pig was chewing his foot. He told his son Ping, "I am waning this year, yet I may not come home again!"

sentences.zh: 」江表傳曰：羽好左氏傳，諷誦略皆上口。〉

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Yu loved the Zuo zhuan; what he recited from memory was largely fluent on the tongue."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang biao zhuan adds that Guan Yu loved the Zuo zhuan and had most of it at the tip of his tongue."

sentences.zh: 子興嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan Xing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 興字安國，少有令問，丞相諸葛亮深器異之。

translations.literal: Xing, courtesy name Anguo, in youth had a fine reputation; Chancellor Zhuge Liang deeply esteemed him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Xing, styled Anguo, was noted for promise in his youth, and Chancellor Zhuge Liang thought him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為侍中、中監軍，數歲卒。

translations.literal: At the capping age he became Palace Attendant and Central Army Supervisor; after several years he died.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he became Palace Attendant and Central Army Supervisor; within a few years he died.

sentences.zh: 子統嗣，尚公主，官至虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: His son Tong succeeded, married a princess, and his office reached Colonel of the Rapid as Tigers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan Tong succeeded, married an imperial princess, and rose to Colonel of the Rapid as Tigers.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，以興庶子彝續封。

translations.literal: He died without sons; Yi's son Yi was continued in the fief.
translations.idiomatic: He died sonless, and the fief passed to Guan Xing's bastard son Guan Yi.

sentences.zh: 〈蜀記曰：龐德子會，隨鍾、鄧伐蜀，蜀破，盡滅關氏家。〉

translations.literal: The Shu Ji states: Pang De's son Pang Hui, following Zhong and Deng on the campaign against Shu, when Shu fell utterly exterminated the Guan clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Ji records that Pang De's son Pang Hui marched with Zhong Hui and Deng Ai against Shu; after the conquest he wiped out every member of the Guan family.

sentences.zh: 張飛字益德，涿郡人也，少與關羽俱事先主。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei, courtesy name Yide, was a native of Zhuo commandery; in youth he together with Guan Yu served the First Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei, styled Yide, came from Zhuo commandery and from his youth served the First Lord alongside Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽年長數歲，飛兄事之。

translations.literal: Yu was several years older; Fei treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu was the elder by a few years, and Zhang Fei honored him as an older brother.

sentences.zh: 先主從曹公破呂布，隨還計，曹公拜飛為中郎將。

translations.literal: When the First Lord followed Lord Cao in defeating Lü Bu, he returned with him to the capital region, and Lord Cao appointed Fei as General of the Gentlemen of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord joined Lord Cao in crushing Lü Bu and accompanied him back to the capital district, Lord Cao named Zhang Fei a General of the Gentlemen of the Household.

sentences.zh: 先主背曹公依袁紹、劉表。

translations.literal: The First Lord turned his back on Lord Cao and attached himself to Yuan Shao and Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord broke with Lord Cao and took refuge first with Yuan Shao, then with Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 表卒，曹公入荊州，先主奔江南。

translations.literal: When Biao died, Lord Cao entered Jing Province; the First Lord fled to the south of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Biao died and Lord Cao took Jing Province, the First Lord bolted for the country south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 曹公追之，一日一夜，及於當陽之長阪。

translations.literal: Lord Cao pursued him one day and one night, catching up at Chang Slope of Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao pressed the pursuit for a day and a night and overtook him at Changban in Dangyang.

sentences.zh: 先主聞曹公卒至，棄妻子走，使飛將二十騎拒後。

translations.literal: The First Lord, hearing that Lord Cao had suddenly arrived, abandoned wife and children and fled, sending Fei with twenty horsemen to hold the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Lord Cao was almost upon him, the First Lord cast aside his family and ran, leaving Zhang Fei with twenty riders to cover the retreat.

sentences.zh: 飛據水斷橋，瞋目橫矛曰：「身是張益德也，可來共決死！

translations.literal: Fei held the bridge across the water, glared, and laid his spear crosswise, saying, "I am Zhang Yide; you may come and fight to the death together!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei took his stand on the bridge, eyes blazing, spear leveled, and shouted, "I am Zhang Yide of Zhuo—who will meet me and fight to the death?"

sentences.zh: 」敵皆無敢近者，故遂得免。

translations.literal: The enemy none dared draw near; therefore they were able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: None of the pursuers dared close with him, and the First Lord slipped away.

sentences.zh: 先主既定江南，以飛為宜都太守、徵虜將軍，封新亭侯，後轉在南郡。

translations.literal: After the First Lord had settled the south of the Long River, he appointed Fei as Grand Administrator of Yidu and General Who Subdues Captives, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xinting, afterward transferring him to Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once the First Lord secured the southern shore, he made Zhang Fei Grand Administrator of Yidu and General Who Subdues Captives, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xinting, and later moved his post to Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 先主入益州，還攻劉璋，飛與諸葛亮等溯流而上，分定郡縣。

translations.literal: When the First Lord entered Yi Province, returned to attack Liu Zhang, Fei together with Zhuge Liang and others went upriver and separately pacified the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord marched into Yi Province, then doubled back against Liu Zhang; Zhang Fei joined Zhuge Liang and the rest in an upstream drive, each column reducing counties along the way.

sentences.zh: 至江州，破璋將巴郡太守嚴顏，生獲顏。

translations.literal: When they reached Jiangzhou they defeated Liu Zhang's general Yan Yan, Grand Administrator of Ba commandery, and captured Yan alive.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangzhou they broke Liu Zhang's officer Yan Yan, Grand Administrator of Ba, and took Yan Yan prisoner.

sentences.zh: 飛呵顏曰：「大軍至，何以不降而敢拒戰？

translations.literal: Fei shouted at Yan, "The great army has arrived—why do you not surrender yet dare to resist in battle?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei roared at him, "The host is here—how dare you refuse surrender and offer battle?"

sentences.zh: 」顏答曰：「卿等無狀，侵奪我州，我州但有斷頭將軍，無有降將軍也。

translations.literal: Yan answered, "You lot behave outrageously, invading and seizing my province; in my province there are only generals who lose their heads, there are no generals who surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yan shot back, "You have no right to trample my province. We breed generals who die—not generals who yield."

sentences.zh: 」飛怒，令左右牽去斫頭，顏色不變，曰：「斫頭便斫頭，何為怒邪！

translations.literal: Fei in anger ordered those at his sides to drag him away and behead him; Yan's expression did not change, saying, "Beheading is beheading—why be angry!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei in fury ordered his men to drag Yan Yan off for execution; Yan never flinched. "Strike off my head if you will—what is there to rage about?"

sentences.zh: 」飛壯而釋之，引為賓客。

translations.literal: Fei admired him and released him, leading him in as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei admired the nerve, cut him loose, and kept him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：初，先主入蜀，至巴郡，顏拊心歎曰：「此所謂獨坐窮山，放虎自衛也！」〉

translations.literal: The Huayang guo zhi states: At first, when the First Lord entered Shu and reached Ba commandery, Yan slapped his breast and sighed, "This is what they call sitting alone on a barren hill and letting loose a tiger to guard yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang guo zhi records that when the First Lord first entered Shu and reached Ba commandery, Yan Yan struck his chest and cried, "They call this sitting on a bare peak and hiring a tiger for a bodyguard!"

sentences.zh: 飛所過戰克，與先主會於成都。

translations.literal: Wherever Fei passed he conquered in battle, and joined the First Lord at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei carried every field he entered and met the First Lord at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 益州既平，賜諸葛亮、法正、飛及關羽金各五百斤，銀千斤，錢五千萬，錦千匹，其餘頒賜各有差，以飛領巴西太守。

translations.literal: When Yi Province was pacified, he granted Zhuge Liang, Fa Zheng, Fei, and Guan Yu each five hundred jin of gold, a thousand jin of silver, fifty million cash, a thousand bolts of brocade; the rest received graded awards; he appointed Fei to act as Grand Administrator of Brazil.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi Province submitted, the First Lord rewarded Zhuge Liang, Fa Zheng, Zhang Fei, and Guan Yu with five hundred jin of gold apiece, a thousand jin of silver, fifty million copper cash, and a thousand rolls of brocade; others were paid on a sliding scale, and Zhang Fei was put in charge of Brazil as Grand Administrator.

sentences.zh: 初，飛雄壯威猛，亞於關羽，魏謀臣程昱等咸稱羽、飛萬人之敵也。

translations.literal: At first, Fei was fierce, mighty, and awe-inspiring, second only to Guan Yu; Wei strategists such as Cheng Yu alike called Yu and Fei a match for ten thousand men each.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei was a tower of martial terror, second only to Guan Yu; Cheng Yu and other Wei counselors spoke of the pair as each worth an army of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 羽善待卒伍而驕於士大夫，飛愛敬君子而不恤小人。

translations.literal: Yu treated common soldiers well but was arrogant toward gentlemen; Fei loved and respected gentlemen but showed no kindness to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu was good to the ranks but haughty with scholars; Zhang Fei revered the cultivated elite yet spared little thought for the men beneath him.

sentences.zh: 先主常戒之曰：「卿刑殺既過差，又日鞭撾健兒，而令在左右，此取禍之道也。

translations.literal: The First Lord often warned him, saying, "Your punishments and killings are already excessive, and daily you flog your stout fighting men yet keep them at your side—this is the road to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord often admonished him: "You kill and maul beyond measure, you daily whip your hardened troopers, then keep them at your elbow—that is how you court ruin."

sentences.zh: 」飛猶不悛。

translations.literal: Fei still did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei would not mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 先主伐吳，飛當率兵萬人，自閬中會江州。

translations.literal: When the First Lord campaigned against Wu, Fei was to lead ten thousand troops from Langzhong to rendezvous at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Lord marched east against Wu, Zhang Fei was to bring ten thousand men from Langzhong to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨發，其帳下將張達、范強殺飛，持其首，順流而奔孫權。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, his camp generals Zhang Da and Fan Qiang killed Fei, took his head, and fled downriver to Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: On the very eve of marching, his subordinate commanders Zhang Da and Fan Qiang murdered him, carried off his head, and raced downcurrent to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 飛營都督表報先主，先主聞飛都督之有表也，曰：「噫！

translations.literal: The camp commandant of Fei's army submitted a memorial reporting to the First Lord; the First Lord, hearing that Fei's commandant had a memorial, said, "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The commandant of Zhang Fei's camp sent up a memorial; when the First Lord heard that a report had come from Zhang Fei's headquarters, he cried, "Ah—

sentences.zh: 飛死矣。

translations.literal: Fei is dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei is gone."

sentences.zh: 」追諡飛曰桓侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the posthumous title Marquis Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously canonized as Marquis Huan.

sentences.zh: 長子苞，早夭。

translations.literal: The eldest son Bao died young.
translations.idiomatic: His firstborn, Zhang Bao, died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 次子紹嗣，官至侍中尚書僕射。

translations.literal: The second son Shao succeeded; his office reached Palace Attendant and Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son Zhang Shao inherited the title and rose to Palace Attendant and Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 苞子遵為尚書，隨諸葛瞻於綿竹，與鄧艾戰，死。

translations.literal: Bao's son Zun became Master of Writing; following Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu, he fought Deng Ai and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao's son Zhang Zun served as Master of Writing; he followed Zhuge Zhan to Mianzhu, met Deng Ai in battle, and fell there.

sentences.zh: 馬超字孟起，右扶風茂陵人也。

translations.literal: Ma Chao, courtesy name Mengqi, was a native of Maoling in You Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao, styled Mengqi, was a man of Maoling in right Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父騰，靈帝末與邊章、韓遂等俱起事於西州。

translations.literal: His father Teng, at the end of Emperor Ling's reign, together with Bian Zhang, Han Sui, and others all raised troops in the western provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ma Teng, late in Emperor Ling's reign, rose with Bian Zhang, Han Sui, and others in the western region.

sentences.zh: 初平三年，遂、騰率眾詣長安。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuping, Sui and Teng led their hosts to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuping 3, Han Sui and Ma Teng brought their armies to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 漢朝以遂為鎮西將軍，遣還金城，騰為征西將軍，遣屯郿。

translations.literal: The Han court appointed Sui as General Who Guards the West and sent him back to Jincheng; Teng as General Who Campaigns West and sent him to encamp at Mei.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court named Han Sui General Who Guards the West and sent him home to Jincheng, while Ma Teng became General Who Campaigns West and was posted at Mei.

sentences.zh: 後騰襲長安，敗走，退還涼州。

translations.literal: Later Teng raided Chang'an, was defeated and fled, withdrawing to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ma Teng struck at Chang'an, was beaten, and fell back to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉鍾繇鎮關中，移書遂、騰，為陳禍福。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Commandant Zhong Yao held the Guanzhong region; he sent letters to Sui and Teng, setting forth fortune and misfortune for them.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Commandant Zhong Yao guarded Guanzhong and wrote to Han Sui and Ma Teng, spelling out the stakes.

sentences.zh: 騰遣超隨繇討郭援、高幹於平陽，超將龐德親斬援首。

translations.literal: Teng sent Chao to follow Yao in campaigning against Guo Yuan and Gao Gan at Pingyang; Chao's general Pang De personally cut off Yuan's head.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng dispatched Ma Chao with Zhong Yao against Guo Yuan and Gao Gan at Pingyang; Ma Chao's officer Pang De himself severed Guo Yuan's head.

sentences.zh: 後騰與韓遂不和，求還京畿。

translations.literal: Later Teng was at odds with Han Sui and requested to return to the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Teng later quarreled with Han Sui, he asked leave to come back to the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 於是徵為衛尉，以超為偏將軍，封都亭侯，領騰部曲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was summoned as Minister of the Guards; Chao was appointed Lieutenant General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Duting, and placed in command of Teng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was then called to court as Minister of the Guards; Ma Chao was made Lieutenant General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Duting, and given his father's command.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：騰字壽成，馬援後也。

translations.literal: The Dian lue states: Teng, courtesy name Shoucheng, was a descendant of Ma Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Dian lue says Ma Teng, styled Shoucheng, traced his line to Ma Yuan.

sentences.zh: 桓帝時，其父字子碩，嘗為天水蘭幹尉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Huan's time, his father, courtesy name Zishuo, once served as captain of Langan in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huan his father, styled Zishuo, had once been captain of Langan in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 後失官，因留隴西，與羌錯居。

translations.literal: Later he lost office and therefore remained in Longxi, dwelling intermixed with the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of his post, he stayed on in Longxi and lived among the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 家貧無妻，遂娶羌女，生騰。

translations.literal: The family was poor and had no wife; therefore he married a Qiang woman and begot Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to marry in the usual way, he took a Qiang wife and fathered Ma Teng.

sentences.zh: 騰少貧無產業，常從彰山中斫材木，負販詣城市，以自供給。

translations.literal: In youth Teng was poor and without property; he often went into the Zhang mountains to cut timber, carried it on his back to peddle in the towns, and so supplied himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng grew up destitute, felled lumber in the Zhang hills, hauled it to market on his back, and lived by that labor.

sentences.zh: 騰為人長八尺餘，身體洪大，面鼻雄異，而性賢厚，人多敬之。

translations.literal: Teng as a man was more than eight chi in height, his body large, his face and nose strikingly bold, yet his nature was worthy and generous, and many people respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng stood over eight chi, broad and imposing of face and nose, yet honest and warm-hearted, and widely respected.

sentences.zh: 靈帝末，涼州刺史耿鄙任信奸吏，民王國等及氐、羌反叛。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ling's reign, Inspector of Liang Province Geng Bi trusted wicked clerks; the people Wang Guo and others together with the Di and Qiang rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Ling's reign, Liangzhou Inspector Geng Bi favored corrupt underlings, and Wang Guo together with Di and Qiang bands rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 州郡募發民中有勇力者，欲討之，騰在募中。

translations.literal: The province and commandery conscripted among the people those who had courage and strength, wishing to campaign against them; Teng was in the levy.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities drafted every stout commoner they could find to put down the rising; Ma Teng was among those levied.

sentences.zh: 州郡異之，署為軍從事，典領部眾。

translations.literal: The province and commandery thought him unusual and appointed him Army Clerk, in charge of leading the host.
translations.idiomatic: They marked him as exceptional, gave him the post of Army Clerk, and put him at the head of a column.

sentences.zh: 討賊有功，拜軍司馬，後以功遷偏將軍，又遷徵西將軍，常屯汧、隴之間。

translations.literal: Campaigning against bandits with merit, he was appointed Army Major; afterward by merit he was promoted to Lieutenant General, then again to General Who Campaigns West, and regularly encamped between Qian and Long.
translations.idiomatic: He earned promotion fighting rebels—Army Major first, then Lieutenant General, then General Who Campaigns West—usually camped between the Qian and Long rivers.

sentences.zh: 初平中，拜徵東將軍。

translations.literal: In the Chuping period he was appointed General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuping years he became General Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 是時，西州少穀，騰自表軍人多乏，求就谷於池陽，遂移屯長平岸頭。

translations.literal: At that time the western provinces were short of grain; Teng himself memorialized that the soldiers were largely in want and requested to draw grain at Chiyang; therefore he moved his camp to the head of the Changping bank.
translations.idiomatic: Grain ran short in the west; Ma Teng petitioned that his troops were starving and asked to forage at Chiyang, then shifted his encampment to the Changping heights.

sentences.zh: 而將王承等恐騰為己害，乃攻騰營。

translations.literal: But generals such as Wang Cheng feared Teng would harm them and therefore attacked Teng's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Generals like Wang Cheng feared he would turn on them and stormed his camp.

sentences.zh: 時騰近出無備，遂破走，西上。

translations.literal: At the time Teng had gone out on a short errand without preparation; therefore he was broken and fled westward.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng was away on a brief trip, caught unprepared, routed, and driven west.

sentences.zh: 會三輔亂，不復來東，而與鎮西將軍韓遂結為異姓兄弟，始甚相親，後轉以部曲相侵入，更為讎敵。

translations.literal: It happened that the Three Adjuncts were in turmoil and he did not come east again, but with General Who Guards the West Han Sui swore brotherhood across surnames; at first they were very intimate, later turned to invading each other's commands and became mutual foes.
translations.idiomatic: The capital districts erupted in chaos, so he never returned east; instead he swore oath-brotherhood with General Who Guards the West Han Sui—first inseparable, then raiding each other's camps until they were bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 騰攻遂，遂走，合眾還攻騰，殺騰妻子，連兵不解。

translations.literal: Teng attacked Sui; Sui fled, gathered his host, returned to attack Teng, killed Teng's wife and children, and their arms would not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng struck Han Sui, who withdrew, rallied, and struck back, slaughtering Ma Teng's family; the fighting would not stop.

sentences.zh: 建安之初，國家綱紀殆弛，乃使司隸校尉鍾繇、涼州牧韋端和解之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jian'an, state discipline was nearly collapsed; therefore they sent Metropolitan Commandant Zhong Yao and Governor of Liang Province Wei Duan to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jian'an the court's grip was failing, so Metropolitan Commandant Zhong Yao and Liangzhou Governor Wei Duan were dispatched to broker peace.

sentences.zh: 徵騰還屯槐裏，轉拜為前將軍，假節，封槐裏侯。

translations.literal: Teng was summoned back to encamp at Huaili, transferred and appointed Forward General, granted the credentials of office, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng was recalled to garrison Huaili, promoted to Forward General, given the baton of authority, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Huaili.

sentences.zh: 北備胡寇，東備白騎，待士進賢，矜救民命，三輔甚安愛之。

translations.literal: To the north he guarded against Hu raiders, to the east against the White Riders; he advanced scholars and cherished the people's lives, and the Three Adjuncts greatly settled and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He watched the northern steppe, watched the White Rider bandits in the east, welcomed talent, and sheltered common lives—so the Three Adjuncts knew peace and loved him.

sentences.zh: 十

translations.literal: Ten.
translations.idiomatic: The tens digit from a broken "fifteen".

translations.literal: (Five).
translations.idiomatic: The ones digit, parenthesized in the source, completes "fifteen" with the preceding entry.

sentences.zh: 年，徵為衛尉，騰自見年老，遂入宿衛。

translations.literal: Years; he was summoned as Minister of the Guards; Teng, seeing himself old, thereupon entered night guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: In that fifteenth year of Jian'an he was summoned as Minister of the Guards; feeling his years, Ma Teng went to the capital to take up palace watch duty.

sentences.zh: 初，曹公為丞相，辟騰長子超，不就。

translations.literal: At first, when Lord Cao was Chancellor, he summoned Teng's eldest son Chao; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Lord Cao first became Chancellor he called Ma Chao, Ma Teng's eldest son, to office; Ma Chao refused.

sentences.zh: 超後為司隸校尉督軍從事，討郭援，為飛矢所中，乃以囊囊其足而戰，破斬援首。

translations.literal: Later Chao became Supervising Army Clerk under the Metropolitan Commandant; campaigning against Guo Yuan, he was struck by a flying arrow, therefore wrapped his foot in a pouch and fought, defeating and beheading Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Supervising Army Clerk to the Metropolitan Commandant, he fought Guo Yuan, took a stray shaft in the foot, bound the wound in leather, and still broke the enemy and took Guo Yuan's head.

sentences.zh: 詔拜徐州刺史，後拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Inspector of Xu Province; afterward he was appointed Grandee Remonstrant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named him Inspector of Xu Province, then Grandee Remonstrant.

sentences.zh: 及騰之入，因詔拜為偏將軍，使領騰營。

translations.literal: When Teng entered, by edict he was appointed Lieutenant General and ordered to lead Teng's camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Teng came to court, an edict made Ma Chao Lieutenant General and put him at the head of his father's troops.

sentences.zh: 又拜超弟休奉車都尉，休弟鐵騎都尉，徙其家屬皆詣鄴，惟超獨留。〉

translations.literal: He also appointed Chao's younger brother Xiu as Bearer of the Gilded Chariot, Xiu's younger brother Tie as Colonel of Agile Cavalry, moved all their family members to Ye, only Chao alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiu was named Bearer of the Gilded Chariot, another brother Ma Tie became Colonel of Agile Cavalry, and the whole household was removed to Ye—only Ma Chao stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 超既統眾，遂與韓遂合從，及楊秋、李堪、成宜等相結，進軍至潼關。

translations.literal: Once Chao commanded the host, he joined in alliance with Han Sui and linked with Yang Qiu, Li Kan, Cheng Yi, and others, advancing the army to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of his father's army Ma Chao allied with Han Sui and with Yang Qiu, Li Kan, Cheng Yi, and the rest, and marched to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 曹公與遂、超單馬會語，超負其多力，陰欲突前捉曹公，曹公左右將許褚瞋目盻之，超乃不敢動。

translations.literal: Lord Cao with Sui and Chao met in talk each on a single horse; Chao relied on his great strength and secretly wished to burst forward and seize Lord Cao; Lord Cao's guard general Xu Chu glared at him, and Chao then did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao met Han Sui and Ma Chao for a parley, each man alone in the saddle; Ma Chao, trusting his strength, meant to rush forward and seize him, but Xu Chu glared from Lord Cao's escort and Ma Chao dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 曹公用賈詡謀，離間超、遂，更相猜疑，軍以大敗。

translations.literal: Lord Cao employed Jia Xu's stratagem to alienate Chao and Sui; they mutually suspected each other, and the army therefore suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao used Jia Xu's ruse to set Ma Chao and Han Sui at odds; mutual suspicion broke them, and their host was shattered.

sentences.zh: 〈山陽公載記曰：初，曹公軍在蒲阪，欲西渡，超謂韓遂曰：「宜於渭北拒之，不過二十日，河東穀盡，彼必走矣。

translations.literal: The Shanyang gong zaiji states: At first, when Lord Cao's army was at Puban, wishing to cross west, Chao said to Han Sui, "We ought to hold them on the north bank of the Wei; not passing twenty days, the grain east of the river will be exhausted and they must flee.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyang gong zaiji records that with Lord Cao stalled at Puban, ready to cross west, Ma Chao urged Han Sui, "Block him north of the Wei: within twenty days his grain from Hedong will give out and he will withdraw."

sentences.zh: 」遂曰：「可聽令渡，蹙於河中，顧不快耶！

translations.literal: Sui said, "We may listen and let them cross, squeeze them in the middle of the river—would that not be swift joy!
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui replied, "Better let him ford and crush him midstream—would that not be sweeter?"

sentences.zh: 」超計不得施。

translations.literal: Chao's plan could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao's plan never got a hearing.

sentences.zh: 曹公聞之曰：「馬兒不死，吾無葬地也。」〉

translations.literal: Lord Cao, hearing it, said, "If that horse-son does not die, I have no burial ground.""
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao said when he heard them, "While that colt of Ma's lives, I shall have nowhere to be buried."

sentences.zh: 超走保諸戎，曹公追至安定，會北方有事，引軍東還。

translations.literal: Chao fled to protect himself among the various Rong; Lord Cao pursued to Anding; it happened that there was trouble in the north, and he led the army back east.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao fled among the western tribes; Lord Cao chased him to Anding, then turned back east when the northern frontier flared up.

sentences.zh: 楊阜說曹公曰：「超有信、布之勇，甚得羌、胡心。

translations.literal: Yang Fu persuaded Lord Cao, saying, "Chao has the courage of Xin and Bu and has won the hearts of the Qiang and Hu deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu warned Lord Cao: "Ma Chao fights like Xin or Peng Yue, and the Qiang and Hu love him.

sentences.zh: 若大軍還，不嚴為其備，隴上諸郡非國家之有也。

translations.literal: If the great army returns and you do not strictly prepare against him, the commanderies on the Long uplands will not belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: If the main force withdraws without leaving iron behind, the Long plateau will not stay yours."

sentences.zh: 」超果率諸戎以擊隴上郡縣，隴上郡縣皆應之，殺涼州刺史韋康，據冀城，有其眾。

translations.literal: Chao indeed led the various Rong to strike the commanderies and counties on the Long uplands; the commanderies and counties on the Long uplands all responded to him; he killed Inspector of Liang Province Wei Kang, occupied Ji city, and possessed his host.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao did exactly that: he swept the Long counties, every district rose for him, he slew Liangzhou Inspector Wei Kang, seized Ji, and took command of the army.

sentences.zh: 超自稱徵西將軍，領並州牧，督涼州軍事。

translations.literal: Chao styled himself General Who Campaigns West, acting Governor of Bing Province, and supervised military affairs of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He declared himself General Who Campaigns West, provisional Governor of Bing Province, and director of Liangzhou military affairs.

sentences.zh: 康故吏民楊阜、姜敘、梁寬、趙衢等，合謀擊超。

translations.literal: Kang's former clerks and people Yang Fu, Jiang Xu, Liang Kuan, Zhao Qu, and others joined in a plot to strike Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Kang's old officers—Yang Fu, Jiang Xu, Liang Kuan, Zhao Qu—conspired against him.

sentences.zh: 阜、敘起於鹵城，超出攻之，不能下；

translations.literal: Fu and Xu rose at Lucheng; Chao went out to attack them and could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu and Jiang Xu rose at Lucheng; Ma Chao besieged them in vain.

sentences.zh: 寬、衢閉冀城門，超不得入。

translations.literal: Kuan and Qu closed the gates of Ji city; Chao could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kuan and Zhao Qu barred the gates of Ji; Ma Chao could not get in.

sentences.zh: 進退狼狽，乃奔漢中依張魯。

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating in dire straits, he then fled to Hanzhong and attached himself to Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between hammer and anvil, he bolted to Hanzhong and threw in with Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 魯不足與計事，內懷於邑，聞先主圍劉璋於成都，密書請降。

translations.literal: Lu was not worth planning affairs with; inwardly he harbored resentment; hearing that the First Lord besieged Liu Zhang at Chengdu, he secretly sent a letter asking to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu was no partner for great designs; Ma Chao brooded in discontent. When he learned the First Lord had Liu Zhang under siege at Chengdu, he sent a secret letter offering defection.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：建安十六年，超與關中諸將侯選、程銀、李堪、張橫、梁興、成宜、馬玩、楊秋、韓遂等，凡十部，俱反，其眾十萬，同據河、潼，建列營陳。

translations.literal: The Dian lue states: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an, Chao together with the Guanzhong generals Hou Xuan, Cheng Yin, Li Kan, Zhang Heng, Liang Xing, Cheng Yi, Ma Wan, Yang Qiu, Han Sui, and others, in all ten divisions, alike rebelled; their host was one hundred thousand; together they held the Yellow River and Tong, establishing camps and battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: The Dian lue records that in Jian'an 16 Ma Chao joined Hou Xuan, Cheng Yin, Li Kan, Zhang Heng, Liang Xing, Cheng Yi, Ma Wan, Yang Qiu, Han Sui, and the rest—ten columns in all—in revolt. A hundred thousand men held the Yellow River line and Tong Pass and threw up entrenchments.

sentences.zh: 是歲，曹公西徵，與超等戰於河、渭之交，超等敗走。

translations.literal: That year Lord Cao campaigned west and fought Chao and the others at the border of the River and the Wei; Chao and the others were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lord Cao marched west and met Ma Chao's coalition where the river meets the Wei; they broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 超至安定，遂奔涼州。

translations.literal: Chao reached Anding, then fled to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao reached Anding, then doubled back into Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔收滅超家屬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the seizure and extermination of Chao's family members.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for the arrest and execution of his entire household.

sentences.zh: 超複敗於隴上。

translations.literal: Chao again was defeated on the Long uplands.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten again on the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 後奔漢中，張魯以為都講祭酒，欲妻之以女，或諫魯曰：「有人若此不愛其親，焉能愛人？

translations.literal: Later he fled to Hanzhong; Zhang Lu made him Libationer Director of Lectures, wished to give him a daughter in marriage; someone remonstrated with Lu, saying, "For a man like this not to love his kin—how can he love others?
translations.idiomatic: He fled once more to Hanzhong. Zhang Lu named him chief lecturer and wanted to marry him to a daughter; an adviser said, "A man who casts off his own blood—how will he cherish yours?"

sentences.zh: 」魯乃止。

translations.literal: Lu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 初，超未反時，其小婦弟種留三輔，及超敗，種先入漢中。

translations.literal: At first, before Chao rebelled, his younger brother-in-law by a concubine, Zhong, remained in the Three Adjuncts; when Chao was defeated, Zhong first entered Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before the revolt, Ma Chao's younger brother-in-law Zhong (born to a concubine) had stayed in the capital districts; when Ma Chao lost, Zhong reached Hanzhung first.

sentences.zh: 正旦，種上壽於超，超搥胸吐血曰：「闔門百口，一旦同命，今二人相賀邪？

translations.literal: On New Year's morning Zhong offered birthday congratulations to Chao; Chao beat his breast and spat blood, saying, "A hundred mouths of one household in one morning shared the same fate—now two men congratulate each other!
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day Zhong came to toast him; Ma Chao hammered his chest until he coughed blood. "A whole clan cut down in a day—and you would raise cups between us two?"

sentences.zh: 」後數從魯求兵，欲北取涼州，魯遣往，無利。

translations.literal: Afterward he repeatedly asked Lu for troops, wishing to go north and take Liang Province; Lu sent him, without profit.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he begged Zhang Lu for soldiers to reconquer Liangzhou; Zhang Lu lent them, to no gain.

sentences.zh: 又魯將楊白等欲害其能，超遂從武都逃入氐中，轉奔往蜀。

translations.literal: Moreover Lu's generals Yang Bai and others wished to harm him for his ability; Chao therefore fled from Wudu into the Di, then turned and ran to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu's officers, Yang Bai among them, plotted against his talent; Ma Chao fled Wudu into Di territory, then doubled toward Shu.

sentences.zh: 是歲建安十九年也。〉

translations.literal: That year was the nineteenth year of Jian'an."
translations.idiomatic: This was Jian'an 19."

sentences.zh: 先主遣人迎超，超將兵徑到城下。

translations.literal: The First Lord sent men to welcome Chao; Chao led troops straight to beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord sent escorts; Ma Chao brought his army right under the walls.

sentences.zh: 城中震怖，璋即稽首，

translations.literal: Those in the city were shaken with terror; Zhang immediately performed the forehead-to-ground obeisance,
translations.idiomatic: Panic seized the city; Liu Zhang kowtowed at once,

sentences.zh: 〈典略曰：備聞超至，喜曰：「我得益州矣。

translations.literal: The Dian lue states: When Bei heard Chao had arrived, he rejoiced and said, "I have gained Yi Province."
translations.idiomatic: The Dian lue says that when Liu Bei learned Ma Chao had come, he exclaimed with joy that Yi Province was now his.

sentences.zh: 」乃使人止超，而潛以兵資之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent men to stop Chao, while secretly supplying him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent orders to hold Ma Chao back, then slipped him reinforcements in secret.

sentences.zh: 超到，令引軍屯城北，超至未一旬而成都潰。〉

translations.literal: When Chao arrived, he ordered him to lead the army and encamp north of the city; Chao had not been there ten days when Chengdu collapsed."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao came up, camped his host north of the walls, and within ten days Chengdu had fallen."

sentences.zh: 以超為平西將軍，督臨沮，因為前都亭侯。

translations.literal: He appointed Chao as General Who Pacifies the West, supervising Linju, and therefore as former Marquis of Duting.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord named Ma Chao General Who Pacifies the West with authority over Linju, confirming his old Marquis of Duting title.

sentences.zh: 〈山陽公載記曰：超因見備待之厚，與備言，常呼備字，關羽怒，請殺之。

translations.literal: The Shanyang gong zaiji states: Because Chao saw that Bei treated him generously, in speaking with Bei he regularly called Bei by his courtesy name; Guan Yu was angry and asked to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyang gong zaiji says Ma Chao, warmed by Liu Bei's kindness, addressed him by his style in conversation; Guan Yu took offense and demanded his life.

sentences.zh: 備曰：「人窮來歸我，卿等怒，以呼我字故而殺之，何以示於天下也！

translations.literal: Bei said, "Men in straits come to attach themselves to me; you are angry and would kill them for calling me by my courtesy name—how would that be shown to the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei said, "The man is destitute and has come to me. Would you execute him for using my familiar name—what sort of signal would that send the world?"

sentences.zh: 」張飛曰：「如是，當示之以禮。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei said, "If so, we ought to show him ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei answered, "Then let us teach him courtesy instead."

sentences.zh: 」明日大會，請超入，羽、飛並杖刀立直，超顧坐席，不見羽、飛，見其直也，乃大驚，遂一不復呼備字。

translations.literal: The next day at the great assembly he invited Chao to enter; Yu and Fei together grasped their swords and stood straight; Chao looked at the seats, did not see Yu and Fei, saw them standing straight, and was greatly startled, and thereafter never again called Bei by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: At the next grand levee they ushered Ma Chao in; Guan Yu and Zhang Fei flanked the hall upright, blades in hand. Ma Chao scanned the banquet and saw only those two rigid figures—no seats for them—and his blood ran cold; from that day he never again used Liu Bei's style to his face.

sentences.zh: 明日歎曰：「我今乃知其所以敗。

translations.literal: The next day he sighed, saying, "I now know the reason I was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The morning after he sighed, "Now I see why I was ruined.

sentences.zh: 為呼人主字，幾為關羽、張飛所殺。

translations.literal: For calling the lord of men by his courtesy name, I was nearly killed by Guan Yu and Zhang Fei.
translations.idiomatic: I dared address my sovereign by his familiar name and nearly died for it at Guan Yu's and Zhang Fei's hands."

sentences.zh: 」自後乃尊事備。

translations.literal: Afterward he then respectfully served Bei.
translations.idiomatic: After that he served Liu Bei with true deference.

sentences.zh: 臣松之按以為超以窮歸備，受其爵位，何容傲慢而呼備字？

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi checks this and considers that Chao, in straits, attached himself to Bei and received his noble rank—how could he be arrogant and call Bei by his courtesy name?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi finds this implausible: Ma Chao came in ruin, accepted rank and stipend from Liu Bei—why would he swagger and call his patron by his style?

sentences.zh: 且備之入蜀，留關羽鎮荊州，羽未嘗在益土也。

translations.literal: Moreover when Bei entered Shu he left Guan Yu to guard Jing Province; Yu had never been in the territory of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when Liu Bei marched into Shu he left Guan Yu on the Jingzhou front; Guan Yu never set foot in Yi.

sentences.zh: 故羽聞馬超歸降，以書問諸葛亮「超人才可誰比類」，不得如書所雲。

translations.literal: Therefore when Yu heard Ma Chao had come to surrender, he wrote to Zhuge Liang asking "to what sort of man Chao's talents may be compared"—it cannot be as the letter says.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Guan Yu, hearing of Ma Chao's defection, wrote Zhuge Liang asking "what manner of man" Ma Chao was—the episode cannot have unfolded as the text claims.

sentences.zh: 羽焉得與張飛立直乎？

translations.literal: How could Yu together with Zhang Fei have stood straight?
translations.idiomatic: How could Guan Yu have stood on ceremony with Zhang Fei in that way?

sentences.zh: 凡人行事，皆謂其可也，知其不可，則不行之矣。

translations.literal: In all human conduct one calls it feasible; knowing it is not feasible, then one does not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Men act when they think a thing right; if they know it wrong, they desist.

sentences.zh: 超若果呼備字，亦謂於理宜爾也。

translations.literal: If Chao indeed called Bei by his courtesy name, he also deemed it proper in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Had Ma Chao truly used Liu Bei's style, he would have believed it justified.

sentences.zh: 就令羽請殺超，超不應聞，但見二子立直，何由便知以呼字之故，雲幾為關、張所殺乎？

translations.literal: Granting that Yu asked to kill Chao, Chao ought not to have heard of it; but seeing only the two sons standing straight, how could he thereby know it was for the reason of calling the courtesy name, saying he was nearly killed by Guan and Zhang?
translations.idiomatic: Even supposing Guan Yu demanded his death, Ma Chao would not have heard the debate; seeing two generals rigid with swords tells him nothing about a quarrel over names—how does that add up to "nearly slain by Guan and Zhang"?

sentences.zh: 言不經理，深可忿疾也。

translations.literal: The words do not accord with reason and are deeply worthy of indignation.
translations.idiomatic: The tale is nonsense, and infuriating nonsense at that.

sentences.zh: 袁暐、樂資等諸所記載，穢雜虛謬，若此之類，殆不可勝言也。〉

translations.literal: The records of Yuan Wei, Yue Zi, and others are filthy, mixed, empty, and false; of this sort, almost they cannot all be spoken."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wei, Yue Zi, and their ilk left a tangle of trash and fabrication; one could not exhaust the list of such errors."

sentences.zh: 先主為漢中王，拜超為左將軍，假節。

translations.literal: When the First Lord became King of Hanzhong, he appointed Chao as General of the Left and granted him the credentials of office.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Lord took the title King of Hanzhong, he named Ma Chao General of the Left and gave him the baton of command.

sentences.zh: 章武元年，遷驃騎將軍，領涼州牧，進封斄鄉侯，策曰：

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhangwu he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, acting Governor of Liang Province, advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Tixiang, the patent reading:
translations.idiomatic: In Zhangwu 1 he rose to General of Agile Cavalry, provisional Governor of Liang Province, and Marquis of Tixiang; the edict of investiture ran:

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，獲繼至尊，奉承宗廟。

translations.literal: We, lacking virtue, have succeeded to the supreme seat and received the charge of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: We lack virtue, yet Heaven has set us on the throne and entrusted us with the house of Han.

sentences.zh: 曹操父子，世載其罪，朕用慘怛，疢如疾首。

translations.literal: Cao Cao and his son, generation after generation bear their crimes; We therefore are grieved and distressed, afflicted as with disease in the head.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao and his heir have piled crime upon crime; Our heart is torn with anguish, Our head aches as from fever.

sentences.zh: 海內怨憤，歸正反本，暨於氐、羌率服，獯鬻慕義。

translations.literal: Within the seas there is resentment and anger; turning to the right and returning to the root; as for the Di and Qiang, they have submitted; the Xiongnu admire righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The realm boils with rage; loyal hearts yearn for the true line; Di and Qiang already bend the knee; northern tribes incline to justice.

sentences.zh: 以君信著北土，威武並昭，是以委任授君，抗颺虓虎，兼董萬里，求民之瘼。

translations.literal: Because your trust is renowned in the northern lands, martial might and awesome virtue together shine; therefore We entrust and commission you, to resist the tiger-like foe, concurrently to oversee ten thousand li, and to seek out the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Your name for good faith rings across the north, and your martial terror is plain to all; We therefore charge you to face the ravening enemy, to watch over distant frontiers, and to learn where the people hurt.

sentences.zh: 其明宣朝化，懷保遠邇，肅慎賞罰，以篤漢祜，以對於天下。

translations.literal: Make clear and spread the court's transforming influence; cherish and protect the far and near; be stern and careful in rewards and punishments, thereby to deepen Han's blessing, thereby to answer the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim Our civilizing rule, shelter near and far alike, wield reward and punishment with care, deepen Heaven's favor to Han, and answer the expectations of the world.

sentences.zh: 二年卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, at age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the reign, forty-seven years old.

sentences.zh: 臨沒上疏曰：「臣門宗二百餘口，為孟德所誅略盡，惟有從弟岱，當為微宗血食之繼，深讬陛下，餘無複言。

translations.literal: Approaching death he submitted a memorial saying, "My clan of more than two hundred mouths was by Mengde almost entirely slaughtered; only my cousin Dai remains, who ought to continue the meager line for sacrifice; I deeply entrust him to Your Majesty; beyond this I have nothing further to say.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he memorialized: "Mengde cut down over two hundred of my kin; only my cousin Ma Dai survives to tend the family altars—I beg Your Majesty to shelter him; I have nothing more to say."

sentences.zh: 」追諡超曰威侯，子承嗣。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the posthumous title Marquis Wei; his son Cheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was canonized posthumously as Marquis Wei; his son Ma Cheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 岱位至平北將軍，進爵陳倉侯。

translations.literal: Dai's rank reached General Who Pacifies the North; his noble rank was advanced to Marquis of Cangcang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dai rose to General Who Pacifies the North and was promoted to Marquis of Cangcang.

sentences.zh: 超女配安平王理。

translations.literal: Chao's daughter was given in marriage to Prince of Anping, Li.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of Ma Chao was married to the Prince of Anping, Liu Li.

sentences.zh: 〈典略曰：初超之入蜀，其庶妻董及子秋，留依張魯。

translations.literal: The Dian lue states: At first when Chao entered Shu, his concubine wife Dong and son Qiu remained and attached themselves to Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Dian lue notes that when Ma Chao first entered Shu, his secondary wife Lady Dong and his son Ma Qiu stayed behind with Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 魯敗，曹公得之，以董賜閻圃，以秋付魯，魯自手殺之。〉

translations.literal: When Lu was defeated, Lord Cao obtained them; he gave Dong to Yan Pu and handed Qiu to Lu; Lu with his own hands killed him."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Lu fell, Lord Cao took them; he gave Lady Dong to Yan Pu and handed Ma Qiu back to Zhang Lu, who killed the boy with his own hands."

sentences.zh: 黃忠字漢升，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Huang Zhong, courtesy name Hansheng, was a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhong, styled Hansheng, was a man of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 荊州牧劉表以為中郎將，與表從子磐共守長沙攸縣。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province Liu Biao appointed him as General of the Gentlemen of the Household; together with Biao's nephew Pan he jointly guarded You county in Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao, Governor of Jing Province, made him a General of the Gentlemen of the Household and sent him with Liu Biao's nephew Liu Pan to hold You county in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 及曹公克荊州，假行裨將軍，仍就故任，統屬長沙守韓玄。

translations.literal: When Lord Cao conquered Jing Province, he was appointed acting General of the Gentlemen of the Household, and still took up his former post, subordinated to Changsha defender Han Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Lord Cao took Jing Province he was named acting Major General and kept his old assignment under Changsha prefect Han Xuan.

sentences.zh: 先主南定諸郡，忠遂委質，隨從入蜀。

translations.literal: When the First Lord pacified the southern commanderies in the south, Zhong thereupon pledged allegiance and followed in entering Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Lord swept the southern shore, Huang Zhong switched sides and followed him into Shu.

sentences.zh: 自葭萌受任，還攻劉璋，忠常先登陷陣，勇毅冠三軍。

translations.literal: From receiving appointment at Jiameng, returning to attack Liu Zhang, Zhong constantly was first to ascend and smash formations; courage and resolution crowned the Three Armies.
translations.idiomatic: From his commission at Jiameng through the campaign against Liu Zhang he was always first over the wall; his valor led the whole host.

sentences.zh: 益州既定，拜為討虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Yi Province was settled, he was appointed General Who Punishes Captives.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi submitted he became General Who Punishes Captives.

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年，於漢中定軍山擊夏侯淵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an, at Dingjun Mountain in Hanzhong he struck Xiahou Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 24 he fought Xiahou Yuan at Dingjun Mountain in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 淵眾甚精，忠推鋒必進，勸率士卒，金鼓振天，歡聲動谷，一戰斬淵，淵軍大敗。
