translations.literal: Yuan's host was very crack; Zhong pushed the spearhead and was sure to advance, encouraged and led the soldiers; gongs and drums shook heaven; joyful cries moved the valleys; in one battle he beheaded Yuan; Yuan's army suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Yuan's troops were picked men; Huang Zhong drove the point of the attack, rallied the ranks, and set drums and cymbals thundering until the hills rang with cheer. In a single clash he cut down Xiahou Yuan and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 遷征西將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Campaigns West.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to General Who Campaigns West.

sentences.zh: 是歲，先主為漢中王，欲用忠為後將軍，諸葛亮說先主曰：「忠之名望，素非關、馬之倫也。

translations.literal: That year, when the First Lord became King of Hanzhong, he wished to employ Zhong as Rear General; Zhuge Liang persuaded the First Lord, saying, "Zhong's fame and standing have never been in the class of Guan and Ma.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as the First Lord prepared to make Huang Zhong Rear General, Zhuge Liang objected: "His reputation has never stood beside Guan Yu's or Ma Chao's."

sentences.zh: 而今便令同列。

translations.literal: Yet now you would order him of the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you would seat him as their equal.

sentences.zh: 馬、張在近，親見其功，尚可喻指；

translations.literal: Ma and Zhang are near; they personally saw his merit; still it may be explained;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao and Zhang Fei are here; they witnessed his deeds and can be reasoned with;

sentences.zh: 關遙聞之，恐必不悅，得無不可乎！

translations.literal: Guan, hearing from afar, I fear will surely be displeased—can this be without problem!
translations.idiomatic: but Guan Yu, far away on the Jing line, is bound to resent it—is that wise?"

sentences.zh: 」先主曰：「吾自當解之。

translations.literal: The First Lord said, "I myself shall explain it.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord said, "I will speak to him myself."

sentences.zh: 」遂與羽等齊位，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was of equal rank with Yu and the others, and granted noble rank as Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: So Huang Zhong was ranked with Guan Yu and the rest and enfeoffed as a Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，追諡剛侯。

translations.literal: The next year he died; posthumously he was given the posthumous title Marquis Gang.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year and was posthumously titled Marquis Gang.

sentences.zh: 子敘，早沒，無後。

translations.literal: His son Xu died young, without posterity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huang Xu died in youth, leaving no heir.

sentences.zh: 趙雲字子龍，常山真定人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Yun, courtesy name Zilong, was a native of Zhending in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun, styled Zilong, came from Zhending in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 本屬公孫瓚，瓚遣先主為田楷拒袁紹，雲遂隨從，為先主主騎。

translations.literal: Originally he belonged to Gongsun Zan; Zan dispatched the First Lord to Tian Kai to resist Yuan Shao, and Yun thereupon followed, serving the First Lord as master of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Gongsun Zan, who sent the First Lord with Tian Kai against Yuan Shao; Zhao Yun joined that column and became the First Lord's cavalry commander.

sentences.zh: 〈雲別傳曰：雲身長八尺，姿顏雄偉，為本郡所舉，將義從吏兵詣公孫瓚。

translations.literal: The Zhao Yun bie zhuan states: Yun's body was eight chi in height; his bearing and appearance were heroic; his commandery recommended him, and leading volunteer clerks and soldiers he went to Gongsun Zan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao Yun bie zhuan says he stood eight chi, cut a martial figure, was recommended by his home commandery, and led a body of volunteers to Gongsun Zan.

sentences.zh: 時袁紹稱冀州牧，瓚深憂州人之從紹也，善雲來附，嘲雲曰：「聞貴州人皆原袁氏，君何獨回心，迷而能反乎？

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Shao styled himself Governor of Ji Province; Zan deeply worried that the people of the province would follow Shao; he was pleased Yun came to attach himself, and mocked Yun, saying, "I have heard the people of your province all incline to the Yuan clan; why alone have you turned your heart—lost yet able to return?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao was calling himself Governor of Ji; Gongsun Zan dreaded losing his people to him, so he welcomed Zhao Yun with a jibe: "They say everyone in your country favors the Yuans—why have you alone switched sides, like a man who loses his way yet finds it again?"

sentences.zh: 」雲答曰：「天下訩訩，未知孰是，民有倒縣之厄，鄙州論議，從仁政所在，不為忽袁公私明將軍也。

translations.literal: Yun answered, "All under Heaven is in turmoil; we do not yet know who is right; the people have the hardship of being hung upside down; in my mean commandery the discussion is to follow where benevolent government is; it is not for slighting the Yuan for private reasons, but to make clear the general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun replied, "The empire is in chaos and the true ruler unclear; the common folk hang by their heels. My neighbors mean only to follow humane government—not to snub the Yuans for private spite, but to declare for a worthy leader."

sentences.zh: 」遂與瓚征討。

translations.literal: Thereupon he campaigned with Zan in expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned under Gongsun Zan.

sentences.zh: 時先主亦依讬瓚，每接納雲，雲得深自結讬。

translations.literal: At the time the First Lord also relied on and attached himself to Zan; each time he received Yun, Yun was able deeply to bind himself in entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord was also under Gongsun Zan's wing; whenever they met, Zhao Yun gave him his deepest pledge.

sentences.zh: 雲以兄喪，辭瓚暫歸，先主知其不反，捉手而別，雲辭曰：「終不背德也。

translations.literal: Yun, because of his elder brother's funeral, took leave of Zan to return for a time; the First Lord knew he would not return, grasped his hand and parted; Yun took leave saying, "In the end I will not betray virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yun went home to mourn his elder brother, the First Lord knew he would not come back to Gongsun Zan; they clasped hands in farewell, and Zhao Yun swore, "I will never break faith with worthy men."

sentences.zh: 」先主就袁紹，雲見於鄴。

translations.literal: The First Lord went to Yuan Shao; Yun met him at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord went over to Yuan Shao, and Zhao Yun joined him at Ye.

sentences.zh: 先主與雲同床眠臥，密遣雲合募得數百人，皆稱劉左將軍部曲，紹不能知。

translations.literal: The First Lord slept together with Yun on one bed, secretly sent Yun to gather recruits and obtained several hundred men, all calling themselves the troops of General Liu the Left; Shao could not know.
translations.idiomatic: They shared a couch while the First Lord secretly sent Zhao Yun to raise several hundred men, all mustered as retainers of "General Liu the Left," under Yuan Shao's nose.

sentences.zh: 遂隨先主至荊州。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed the First Lord to Jing Province."
translations.idiomatic: From there Zhao Yun followed the First Lord to Jing Province."

sentences.zh: 及先主為曹公所追於當陽長阪，棄妻子南走，雲身抱弱子，即後主也，保護甘夫人，即後主母也，皆得免難。

translations.literal: When the First Lord was pursued by Lord Cao at Chang Slope of Dangyang, abandoned wife and children and fled south, Yun himself embraced the weak child—that is, the Later Lord—and protected Lady Gan—that is, the Later Lord's mother—and all obtained exemption from disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Lord Cao ran the First Lord down at Changban in Dangyang, the First Lord cast aside his family and fled south; Zhao Yun carried the infant who would become the Later Lord and shielded Lady Gan, the boy's mother, and brought them through unscathed.

sentences.zh: 遷為牙門將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Ivory Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Ivory Gates.

sentences.zh: 先主入蜀，雲留荊州。

translations.literal: When the First Lord entered Shu, Yun remained in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Lord marched into Shu, Zhao Yun stayed behind in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 〈雲別傳曰：初，先主之敗，有人言雲已北去者，先主以手戟擿之曰：「子龍不棄我走也。

translations.literal: The Zhao Yun bie zhuan states: At first, when the First Lord was defeated, someone said Yun had already gone north; the First Lord with a hand halberd stabbed and said, "Zilong will not abandon me and flee.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao Yun bie zhuan records that after the rout someone claimed Zhao Yun had ridden north to the enemy; the First Lord flung a halberd and cried, "Zilong would never desert me!"

sentences.zh: 」頃之，雲至。

translations.literal: In a short while Yun arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later Zhao Yun appeared.

sentences.zh: 從平江南，以為偏將軍，領桂陽太守，代趙範。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of the south of the Long River, he was appointed Lieutenant General and placed in charge as Grand Administrator of Guilin, replacing Zhao Fan.
translations.idiomatic: After the south shore was secured he became Lieutenant General and Grand Administrator of Guilin, succeeding Zhao Fan.

sentences.zh: 範寡嫂曰樊氏，有國色，範欲以配雲。

translations.literal: Fan's widowed sister-in-law surnamed Fan had national-level beauty; Fan wished to give her to Yun in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fan offered him his widowed sister-in-law, a Lady Fan of legendary beauty, as a wife.

sentences.zh: 雲辭曰：「相與同姓，卿兄猶我兄。

translations.literal: Yun declined, saying, "We are of the same surname; your elder brother is like my elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun refused: "We share a surname; your elder brother is my elder brother.

sentences.zh: 」固辭不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and would not permit.
translations.idiomatic: He stood firm and would not take her.

sentences.zh: 時有人勸雲納之，雲曰：「範迫降耳，心未可測；

translations.literal: At the time someone urged Yun to take her; Yun said, "Fan was forced to surrender; his heart cannot yet be fathomed;
translations.idiomatic: Others pressed him to accept; he said, "Zhao Fan surrendered under duress; his loyalties are untested;

sentences.zh: 天下女不少。

translations.literal: there are not few women under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: and the world holds no shortage of women."

sentences.zh: 」遂不取。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not take her.
translations.idiomatic: So he let the match drop.

sentences.zh: 範果逃走，雲無纖介。

translations.literal: Fan indeed fled; Yun had not the slightest grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fan bolted soon after, yet Zhao Yun bore him no ill will.

sentences.zh: 先是，與夏侯惇戰於博望，生獲夏侯蘭。

translations.literal: Earlier, he had fought Xiahou Dun at Bowang and captured Xiahou Lan alive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at Bowang, he had faced Xiahou Dun and taken Xiahou Lan prisoner.

sentences.zh: 蘭是雲鄉里人，少小相知，雲白先主活之，薦蘭明於法律，以為軍正。

translations.literal: Lan was a fellow townsman of Yun; they knew each other from youth; Yun reported to the First Lord to spare him alive, recommended Lan as clear on statutes and law, and appointed him Army Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Lan was a countryman he had known since boyhood; Zhao Yun begged the First Lord to spare him, then recommended him as expert in statute law and had him named Army Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 雲不用自近，其慎慮類如此。

translations.literal: Yun did not employ him to draw near himself; his cautious deliberation was of this class.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Xiahou Lan at arm's length rather than exploit a private tie—such was his caution.

sentences.zh: 先主入益州，雲領留營司馬。

translations.literal: When the First Lord entered Yi Province, Yun acted as Camp Marshal of the Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Lord entered Yi, Zhao Yun served as Camp Marshal of the rear headquarters.

sentences.zh: 此時先主孫夫人以權妹驕豪，多將吳吏兵，縱橫不法。

translations.literal: At this time the First Lord's Lady Sun, because she was Sun Quan's younger sister, was arrogant and fierce, and led many Wu clerks and soldiers, running rampant unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord's wife, Lady Sun—Sun Quan's sister—was haughty and headstrong, surrounded by Wu officers who ran wild and broke every rule.

sentences.zh: 先主以雲嚴重，必能整齊，特任掌內事。

translations.literal: Because the First Lord considered Yun stern and weighty, sure to be able to set in order, he specially entrusted him to manage inner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord, trusting Zhao Yun's gravity, gave him charge of the inner household to keep order.

sentences.zh: 權聞備西徵，大遣舟船迎妹，而夫人內欲將後主還吳，雲與張飛勒兵截江，乃得後主還。〉

translations.literal: When Quan heard Bei was campaigning west, he greatly sent boats and ships to welcome his younger sister, while the lady inwardly wished to take the Later Lord back to Wu; Yun together with Zhang Fei led troops to intercept on the river, and only then obtained the Later Lord's return."
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan learned that Liu Bei had marched west, he sent a fleet to fetch his sister; she meant to carry the young heir back to Wu. Zhao Yun and Zhang Fei blocked the river with arms and forced the boy's return."

sentences.zh: 七年卒，追諡順平侯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; posthumously he was given the posthumous title Marquis Shunping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of the reign and received the posthumous title Marquis Shunping.

sentences.zh: 初，先主時，惟法正見諡；

translations.literal: At first, in the First Lord's time, only Fa Zheng received a posthumous title;
translations.idiomatic: Under the First Lord only Fa Zheng had been granted a posthumous name;

sentences.zh: 後主時，諸葛亮功德蓋世，蔣琬、費禕荷國之重，亦見諡；

translations.literal: in the Later Lord's time, Zhuge Liang's merit and virtue covered the age, Jiang Wan and Fei Yi bore the state's heavy weight, and they also received posthumous titles;
translations.idiomatic: under the Later Lord, Zhuge Liang—whose service outshone the age—along with Jiang Wan and Fei Yi, pillars of the state, were likewise canonized;

sentences.zh: 陳祗寵待，特加殊獎，夏侯霸遠來歸國，故複得諡；

translations.literal: Chen Zhi received favor and treatment, specially receiving extraordinary awards; Xiahou Ba came from afar to return to the state, therefore again received a posthumous title;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi won singular favor; Xiahou Ba defected from afar—each earned a posthumous style;

sentences.zh: 於是關羽、張飛、馬超、龐統、黃忠及雲乃追諡，時論以為榮。

translations.literal: thereupon Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Pang Tong, Huang Zhong, and Yun were posthumously titled; contemporary discussion deemed it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: and only then were Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Pang Tong, Huang Zhong, and Zhao Yun honored posthumously—an accolade the age thought fitting.

sentences.zh: 〈雲別傳載後主詔曰：「雲昔從先帝，功積既著。

translations.literal: The Zhao Yun bie zhuan carries the Later Lord's edict stating, "Yun in former times followed the First Emperor; his accumulated merit was already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao Yun bie zhuan preserves an edict of the Later Lord: "Zhao Yun followed my imperial father and piled deed upon deed.

sentences.zh: 朕以幼沖，涉塗艱難，賴恃忠順，濟於危險。

translations.literal: We, being young and tender, traveled a hard road; relying on loyal obedience, We crossed through danger.
translations.idiomatic: We were a child on a perilous road; it was his steadfast loyalty that bore Us through.

sentences.zh: 夫諡所以敘元勳也，外議雲宜諡。

translations.literal: Posthumous titles are the means to narrate the chief founders of merit; outside discussion holds that Yun ought to receive a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous names exist to crown the founders of the realm; the court agrees Zhao Yun should have one."

sentences.zh: 」大將軍姜維等議，以為雲昔從先帝，勞績既著，經營天下，遵奉法度，功效可書。

translations.literal: General-in-chief Jiang Wei and others deliberated, holding that Yun in former times followed the First Lord; his labor and traces were already manifest; ordering and managing all under Heaven, he honored and observed the statutes; his merit and efficacy could be written.
translations.idiomatic: General Jiang Wei and his colleagues argued that Zhao Yun had served the First Lord with conspicuous toil, helped order the realm within the law, and left a record worth carving in bronze.

sentences.zh: 當陽之役，義貫金石，忠以衛上，君念其賞，禮以厚下，臣忘其死。

translations.literal: At the Dangyang affair, righteousness pierced metal and stone; with loyalty he guarded his lord; the lord remembered his reward; with ritual he treated inferiors; ministers forgot death.
translations.idiomatic: At Changban his fidelity rang like metal and stone—loyalty that shielded his sovereign, a sovereign mindful of reward, a minister who honored his men and faced death undaunted.

sentences.zh: 死者有知，足以不朽；

translations.literal: If the dead have knowledge, it is enough to be imperishable;
translations.idiomatic: If the dead know, they need no richer immortality;

sentences.zh: 生者感恩，足以殞身。

translations.literal: if the living feel gratitude, it is enough to give up body.
translations.idiomatic: if the living remember, they owe him their lives."

sentences.zh: 謹按諡法，柔賢慈惠曰順，執事有班曰平，克定禍亂曰平，應諡雲曰順平侯。〉

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the law of posthumous titles, soft worthiness with kind grace is called shun; holding office with order is called ping; being able to settle calamity and disorder is called ping; responding to posthumous title for Yun is Marquis Shunping."
translations.idiomatic: By the canons of ennoblement, gentle worth and merciful grace are "shun," ordered service is "ping," and quelling chaos is "ping"; together they yield the title Marquis Shunping for Zhao Yun."

sentences.zh: 雲子統嗣，官至虎賁中郎，督行領軍。

translations.literal: Yun's son Tong succeeded; his office reached Colonel of the Rapid as Tigers and acting Leader of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Tong inherited the rank, rising to Colonel of the Rapid as Tigers and acting Leader of the Army.

sentences.zh: 次子廣，牙門將，隨姜維遝中，臨陳戰死。

translations.literal: The second son Guang, General of the Ivory Gates, followed Jiang Wei in Tazhong and died in battle on the lines.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Zhao Guang, a General of the Ivory Gates, followed Jiang Wei to Tazhong and died on the field.

translations.literal: The rubric heading reads "Appraisal" (評).
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal.

sentences.zh: 評曰：關羽、張飛皆稱萬人之敵，為世虎臣。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Guan Yu and Zhang Fei were both called a match for ten thousand men each, and were tiger-like ministers of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's judgment: Guan Yu and Zhang Fei were each worth an army of ten thousand—tigers among men of their day.

sentences.zh: 羽報效曹公，飛義釋嚴顏，並有國士之風。

translations.literal: Yu repaid merit to Lord Cao; Fei in righteousness released Yan Yan; both had the air of knights of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu repaid Lord Cao with a deed of arms; Zhang Fei spared Yan Yan out of principle—both showed the temper of true champions.

sentences.zh: 然羽剛而自矜，飛暴而無恩，以短取敗，理數之常也。

translations.literal: Yet Yu was rigid and self-conceited; Fei was violent and without kindness; by their shortcomings they brought defeat—it is the constant pattern of principle and fate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guan Yu's stubborn pride and Zhang Fei's savage disregard for others' lives were their undoing—a law as old as fate itself.

sentences.zh: 馬超阻戎負勇，以覆其族，惜哉！

translations.literal: Ma Chao relied on the Rong tribes and trusted his courage, thereby destroying his clan—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao staked everything on steppe allies and his own bravado until his house was swept away—what a waste.

sentences.zh: 能因窮致泰，不猶愈乎！

translations.literal: To be able, starting from poverty, to reach security—is that not still better!
translations.idiomatic: To rise from destitution to a steady place under Heaven—is that not the better path!

sentences.zh: 黃忠、趙雲強摯壯猛，並作爪牙，其灌、滕之徒歟？

translations.literal: Huang Zhong and Zhao Yun were strong, resolute, mighty, and fierce; together they became claws and fangs; are they perhaps of the class of Guan Ying and the Lord of Teng?
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhong and Zhao Yun—iron-hard, lion-bold, the sovereign's talons—do they not belong in the company of Guan Ying and the Lord of Teng?
